newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar cabinet resigns as president takes office.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar cabinet resigns as president takes office.

text.p: Madagascar's prime minister offered his government's resignation on Saturday on the eve of President Didier Ratsiraka's formal assumption of office.
Prime Minister Norbert Ratsirahonana made the announcement himself in a broadcast to the nation when he confirmed imminent salary increases for public and private sector workers.
The resignation was a formality, intended to leave Ratsiraka, 60, the freedom to pick his own cabinet team.
In the meantime Ratsirahonana and his ministers will remain in day-to-day charge of government business.
On January 31 Ratsiraka was declared narrow winner of the presidential run-off election held last December 29, gaining revenge over ex-president Albert Zafy.
Zafy won the island's first multi-party polls in 1993, ending Ratsiraka's 18-year rule.
Officials said President Joaquim Chissano of Mozambique and senior dignitaries from Algeria, France, Libya, Mauritius and the World Bank would attend Sunday's ceremony.
The managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Michel Camdessus, sent Ratsiraka a long message of congratulations, officials said.

Camdessus advised the incoming president of one of the world's poorest countries to "pursue healthy financial policies as the only way left to Madagascar to create, at last, a suitable framework for development and the well-being of its people."
For most of his first period in the presidency Ratsiraka was a convinced Marxist whose policies helped wrecked the economy of the world's fourth-largest island.
